# 🧮 The order generated by a column of the SU(n)_k S-matrix — code and data

Companion material for *The order generated by a column of the $\mathrm{SU}(n)_k$ $S$-matrix is
locally a numerical semigroup ring. Part I: Gauss sums, power sums of the spectrum, and Gorenstein
columns* (Carles Marín), deposited on Zenodo:
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.22848529](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22848529). That is the **concept
DOI** — it always resolves to the current version — and it carries the note in both editions,
English and Spanish.

Both PDFs are here too — `P3a.pdf` and `P3a_es.pdf`, byte for byte the files deposited on Zenodo —
together with the tool `P3a.py`, the scripts behind every number the note calls *measured*, and
their archived output.

It lives in this repository, next to [`segmento/`](../segmento) and [`conductor/`](../conductor),
because it is the same question asked of a different element: [`segmento/`](../segmento) computes
the ring of character values at the principal element — the column $\mu=0$ of the modular
$S$-matrix, whose entries are the quantum dimensions — and this note computes it at **every**
column.

## 🎯 What the note proves

Fix a column $\mu$ of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathrm{SU}(n)_k$ and let $A_\mu$ be the ring
generated by the Verlinde eigenvalues $S_{\lambda\mu}/S_{0\mu}$ — by Kac–Peterson, the values of the
characters of $\mathrm{SU}(n)$ at the element of finite order $g_\mu$. The *field* has been known
since Pianzola 1987, and for modular data since Gannon–Schopieray 2019. Here is the **ring**, at
prime height $p=n+k$.

1. **The decomposition.** $A_\mu=\mathcal O_{\mathbb Q(\zeta_m)}\otimes C_T$: the integers of the
   cyclotomic field fixed by the charge of $\mu$ under the centre, tensored with an order $C_T$ that
   depends only on the reduced spectrum $T\subset\mathbb F_p$ of $g_\mu$.
2. **The ring is monomial.** Locally at $p$, the valuations of $C_T$ form a **numerical semigroup**
   $S_T$, written down exactly by Gauss sums and Stickelberger's theorem.
3. **Everything is then read in $S_T$.** The index is $[\mathcal O_\mu:A_\mu]=p^{\varphi(m)\delta}$
   with $\delta$ the number of gaps; $A_\mu$ is **Gorenstein** if and only if $S_T$ is symmetric;
   $p\,\mathcal O_\mu\subseteq A_\mu$ when the conductor is at most the ramification index;
   level–rank duality replaces $T$ by its negated complement and keeps $S_T$; the vacuum column has
   $S_T=\mathbb N_0$ and its order is maximal.
4. **And $S_T$ is read inside $\mathbb F_p$.** It is generated by $e=(p-1)/h$ together with the
   $j<e$ with $M_{hj}(T)\neq0$, where $M_r(T)=\sum_{t\in T}t^r$ and $h$ is the order of the
   multiplicative stabiliser of $T$ — proved for $p>(n-1)(n-2)$, and measured for every $p$ when
   $n\le12$. At prime height the first non-Gorenstein column, by $n$ and then by level, is
   $\mathrm{SU}(5)_{12}$.

The index alone does not see the difference: at $\mathrm{SU}(7)_{22}$ the columns
$\mu=(0,0,1,0,2,5)$ and $\mu=(0,0,0,6,2,5)$ both have index $29^{6\cdot3}$, and only one of them is
Gorenstein. The semigroup sees it.

## 🧪 How to doubt a number

```
python P3a.py autotest
```

recomputes from nothing the worked examples of the note — the first non-Gorenstein column
$\mathrm{SU}(5)_{12}$, the maximal vacuum, the index as the number of gaps on every orbit with
$p\le13$, the two $\mathrm{SU}(6)_{11}$ columns with the same conformal weight and different
semigroups, level–rank, the trinomial $X^5+2X+27$ at $p=67$, the non-Gorenstein column at composite
height 14 — runs a decoy that must fail, exercises every guard, and ends with
`SELF-TEST: all correct` (about 25 seconds; the archived run is `autotest_OUT.txt`).

One column at a time:

```
python P3a.py columna 7 22 0 0 1 0 2 5      # spectrum, moments, S_T, index, Gorenstein
python P3a.py espectro 29 1 4 5 7 8 9 24    # the semigroup of a centred spectrum
python P3a.py maximales 17 5                # maximal columns, closed formula and enumeration
```

It computes the index and the conductor a **second** way as well, as indices of integer lattices,
without the semigroup — and it declines, rather than guessing, when the height is not an odd prime,
when a $p$-adic lift it cannot resolve could change $S_T$, or when the cyclotomic field is too large
for exact lattice arithmetic.

## 🚧 Part II

The $p$-adic anatomy of the fusion ring — the $p$-valuation of Gepner's discriminant as
ramification, defects and gluing — is the sequel, and is not here.

## 🚫 What is deliberately not here

The correspondence around this line of work does not travel with it, held out **by location, not by
a list of names**. A check refuses to release a bundle in which anything imports or reads a file
that is not in it; this bundle passes it.
